title: Conviction of Sin
definition: Conviction of sin is the Holy Spirit's work of exposing guilt, unbelief, righteousness, and judgment so people may turn to Christ.
summary: The Spirit convicts sinners and believers, leading them toward truth and repentance.
christFocus: Jesus promised that the Spirit would convict the world and glorify Him as the only Savior.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Conviction is not hopeless condemnation. It is the Spirit's gracious work of bringing truth to the conscience and heart. He exposes sin so people may stop hiding and turn to God.

For unbelievers, conviction reveals the need for Christ. For believers, conviction leads to confession, repentance, cleansing, and renewed obedience.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People often confuse conviction with shame or ignore conviction until the conscience hardens. This doctrine matters because conviction is a mercy that leads to life.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Respond quickly when the Spirit convicts through Scripture. Confess sin, trust Christ's mercy, and take concrete steps of repentance.
